🌍 Global Security Outlook – 10 October 2025

⸻

AFRICA

🇨🇲 Cameroon – Thousands rallied in Maroua supporting opposition candidate Issa Tchiroma Bakary ahead of the presidential election, as 92-year-old President Paul Biya seeks to extend his 43-year rule.
🇲🇱 Mali – Fuel shortages continue in Bamako as al-Qa’ida-linked militants maintain a blockade, paralyzing transport and commerce.
🇸🇳 Senegal – A rare Rift Valley Fever outbreak has killed 17, prompting heightened public-health surveillance and livestock controls.

⸻

EAST ASIA & PACIFIC

🇰🇭 / 🇹🇭 Cambodia / Thailand – Roughly 100 Cambodians protested near the Sa Kaeo border against Thai plans to evict villagers during land-mine clearance operations.
🇵🇭 Philippines – A second major offshore quake (M 6.9) struck the southern region hours after a 7.4-magnitude event killed at least five, raising aftershock and landslide risks.

⸻

EUROPE

🇧🇪 Belgium – Police arrested three suspects accused of plotting a drone-borne explosive attack on senior politicians, including Prime Minister Bart De Wever.
🇬🇪 Georgia – Authorities detained 13 people after post-election unrest in Tbilisi as the government clamps down on protests.
🇪🇸 Spain – National grid operator Red Eléctrica warned of possible rolling blackouts following two weeks of severe voltage instability.

⸻

MIDDLE EAST & NORTH AFRICA

🇮🇱 / 🇵🇸 Israel / Palestinian Territories – Displaced Gazans began returning to damaged homes after a ceasefire took effect and Israeli forces partially withdrew.
🇲🇦 Morocco – Youth-led demonstrations continued, urging King Mohammed VI to dismiss Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch and enact long-promised reforms.

⸻

SOUTH & CENTRAL ASIA

🇦🇫 / 🇮🇳 Afghanistan / India – Multiple explosions rocked Kabul as the Taliban intensified diplomatic outreach to New Delhi; casualty details remain unclear.
🇵🇰 Pakistan – Islamabad and Rawalpindi entered full lockdown ahead of a Tehreek-e-Labbaik rally, with roads sealed and communications restricted amid fears of clashes.

⸻

WESTERN HEMISPHERE

🇨🇴 Colombia – The government executed an $11.2 billion domestic debt swap, its largest ever, to ease fiscal pressures.
🇨🇷 Costa Rica – Lawmakers scheduled an October 20 review of efforts to strip President Chaves of legal immunity.
🇪🇨 Ecuador – Widespread strikes and roadblocks over diesel-price hikes intensified, challenging President Noboa’s administration.
🇬🇹 Guatemala – Proposed anti-gang legislation includes building a high-security prison and imposing harsher sentences as murder rates climb.
🇵🇪 Peru – Congress advanced impeachment proceedings against President Dina Boluarte following late-night cross-party votes.

⸻

End of Brief

Students for a Democratic Society at the University of Illinois Chicago held a protest yesterday calling for a “sanctuary campus.”

Look closer. One protester with pink hair is holding an Anakbayan banner, the youth arm of Bayan, which is linked to the Communist Party of the Philippines and its armed guerilla wing, the New People’s Army, both U.S.-designated terrorist organizations. Another waves a Che Guevara flag.

A perfect snapshot of what campus activism looks like in 2025 America.
